notes: Historical facts (FY2023–25): revenue and income from operations (used as EBIT), depreciation & amortization, and capex components are taken from Meta’s FY2025 Form 10-K consolidated statements. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003942/meta-20251231.htm))

Capex definition: capex is modeled as purchases of property and equipment plus principal payments on finance leases (Meta’s disclosed FCF construction), using absolute cash outflow components from the cash flow statement. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003942/meta-20251231.htm))

NWC definition (simplified for DCF QA): NWC = (Total current assets − cash and cash equivalents − marketable securities) − Total current liabilities, where “marketable securities” are treated as investments excluded from operating working capital. This yields negative NWC for FY2023–25. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003942/meta-20251231.htm))

Base-case forecast drivers (FY2026–30) are modeling assumptions, not company guidance; they are chosen to be consistent with management’s FY2026 capex step-up ($115B–$135B) while allowing gradual capex intensity normalization thereafter. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003832/meta-12312025xexhibit991.htm))

Tax rate: base-case tax_rate uses the midpoint of management’s FY2026 expected tax rate range (13%–16%). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003832/meta-12312025xexhibit991.htm))
WACC (0.085) and terminal growth (0.02) are independent valuation assumptions for the DCF pipeline (not explicitly disclosed by the company).

NOLs: nol_balance includes US federal and state net operating loss carryforwards (sum of reported balances). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003942/meta-20251231.htm))

NOL utilization percent (0.80) is assumed; the filing describes utilization constraints/limitations but does not provide a single deterministic utilization rate for valuation use. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003942/meta-20251231.htm))

Comps: forward P/E (P/E NTM) is sourced from StockAnalysis; EV/NTM revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA were left null due to lack of reliably accessible NTM-specific EV multiples in the referenced free sources.

catalysts: Evidence that operating income remains above 2025 as FY2026 infrastructure investment ramps into run-rate.
Sustained ad monetization (ad impressions and average price per ad) despite privacy/regulatory constraints.
Capex normalization (or better-than-feared ROI) leading to improving free cash flow conversion over time.
Regulatory developments (EU/US) that reduce uncertainty around ad delivery/product constraints.
company_overview: Meta reports two segments: Family of Apps (advertising placements on its platforms) and Reality Labs. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003942/meta-20251231.htm))

Substantially all revenue is generated from advertising, primarily from Facebook and Instagram, with marketer spend tied to delivering ad impressions/actions. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003942/meta-20251231.htm))

Management is positioning growth and platform relevance around AI (“superintelligence”) and continued investment in immersive technologies. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003832/meta-12312025xexhibit991.htm))
current_context: Q1 2026 total revenue guidance is $53.5B–$56.5B; guidance assumes an approximately 4% FX tailwind. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003832/meta-12312025xexhibit991.htm))

FY2026 total expenses guidance is $162B–$169B, with infrastructure costs and higher depreciation/infrastructure opex as key drivers. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003832/meta-12312025xexhibit991.htm))

FY2026 capex (including principal payments on finance leases) is guided to $115B–$135B; management expects operating income above 2025 despite the step-up. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003832/meta-12312025xexhibit991.htm))
Absent changes to the tax landscape, FY2026 tax rate is expected to be 13%–16%. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003832/meta-12312025xexhibit991.htm))
investment_highlights: Base case assumes high-teen revenue growth in 2026 that decelerates gradually, consistent with recent momentum yet reflective of a large AI investment cycle.
EBIT margin is modeled to stabilize in the high-40s/low-40s range (as a decimal margin around ~0.42), supported by scale efficiencies even with higher depreciation and infrastructure costs.
Capex intensity is front-loaded (peak in 2026–27) and then tapers, translating the near-term AI buildout into a more normal long-run reinvestment profile.
Working capital remains a structural tailwind (negative NWC under an excluding-cash/marketable-securities definition), reducing required incremental funding as growth continues.
Tax capacity is supported by NOL carryforwards; utilization is modeled at 80% in the base case.
key_risks: Advertising revenue sensitivity to user data/tax/privacy changes, regulatory outcomes, and platform measurement limitations. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003942/meta-20251231.htm))
AI/infrastructure investment may be less productive than expected, pressuring EBIT margins via higher opex/depreciation before returns materialize.
Working capital definition and magnitude can deviate materially from the simplified DCF NWC construction.
Tax rate volatility and/or NOL utilization limitations due to legislative change and ownership-change restrictions.

presentation.subtitle: Meta Platforms (META): DCF Inputs (FY2023–25 actuals; FY2026–30 base case)
valuation_summary: The DCF base case is anchored to audited FY2023–25 financials and then uses sober forward assumptions (revenue growth, margin, and investment intensity) consistent with management’s FY2026 capex and expense guidance. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003942/meta-20251231.htm))
Terminal value is computed using Gordon Growth (terminal growth 2.0%) with an 8.5% WACC to reflect long-run, mature-market economics rather than a short-duration growth spike.
Peer cross-check uses forward P/E for relevant internet/advertising-attention peers; EV/NTM multiples are left null where NTM inputs were not reliably available from the referenced free sources.
